| Buyer situation | Starting shortlist | Why these tools merit evaluation | First disqualifying issue to test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small, streamlined service operation | [Jobber](#jobber), [Housecall Pro](#housecall-pro), [ServiceM8](#servicem8) | Test a focused request-to-payment workflow without assuming equivalent devices, packaging, or growth capacity. | Devices, user limits, package fit, and any workflow beyond straightforward service. |
| Growing multi-crew trade business | [Simpro](#simpro), [FieldEdge](#fieldedge), [FieldPulse](#fieldpulse) | Test dispatch, field roles, office handoffs, permissions, and reporting. | Migration, onboarding, seats, and the package each role needs. |
| Combined service and project contractor | [Simpro](#simpro), [BuildOps](#buildops), [ServiceTitan](#servicetitan) | Run one service job and one project through all three. Test purchasing, costing, change management, and progress billing separately. | Project depth, accounting or ERP behavior, implementation ownership, and commercial scope. |
| Commercial or asset-heavy operation | [Simpro](#simpro), [Joblogic](#joblogic), [BuildOps](#buildops) | Test assets, recurring work, purchasing, commercial jobs, and project controls. | Asset history, offline behavior, accounting boundaries, and configuration ownership. |
| Recurring maintenance operation | [Simpro](#simpro), [Joblogic](#joblogic), [FieldEdge](#fieldedge) | Use this shortlist to test recurring schedules, service history, agreements, failed-inspection follow-up, and billing under the same scenario. | Failed-inspection follow-up, asset records, field resync, agreement-cycle handling, and reporting. |

| Tool | Operating model | Team and workflow complexity | Orientation | Principal mismatch | First demo test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Simpro](#simpro) | Connected service and project work | Growing, multi-role operation | Trade service and projects | The buying case stops at basic scheduling | One service job and one project from estimate through reporting, including migrated customer, job, and asset data |
| [Jobber](#jobber) | Quote-to-payment service work | Small or streamlined team | Service business | The demonstrated tier, user, promotion, or billing terms fail the buying policy | Booking through payment, including users and add-ons |
| [Joblogic](#joblogic) | Asset-led reactive and recurring work | Multi-role maintenance team | Service and maintenance | The accounting workflow fails the buyer's live test | Offline asset job through resync and accounting |
| [FieldEdge](#fieldedge) | Dispatch and service agreements | Growing service team | Field service trades | The demonstrated commercial model fails the buying policy | Agreement job through dispatch, invoice, and reporting |
| [BuildOps](#buildops) | Commercial service and projects | Complex commercial operation | Commercial specialty contracting | The demonstrated workflow is too complex for the buying case | Maintenance job and project through the actual ERP |
| [ServiceTitan](#servicetitan) | Technician-led service workflows | Scaling, implementation-ready team | Field and home service | The buyer has little internal implementation capacity | Call through invoice with a reassignment, permission change, and failed integration sync |
| [FieldPulse](#fieldpulse) | Office-to-field job workflows | Growing team with distinct roles | Field service | The demonstrated access and pricing model does not fit | Permissions and handoffs for every role |
| [Housecall Pro](#housecall-pro) | Customer-to-payment home service | Small or growing team | Home service | The demonstrated workflow lacks needed project, asset, inventory, or multi-entity depth | Complete customer and technician journey with a reschedule |
| [Service Fusion](#service-fusion) | Multi-user service workflow | Small-to-midsize service company | Field service | The demonstrated workflow is too broad or too shallow for the buying case | Estimate-to-payment job plus accounting error recovery |
| [ServiceM8](#servicem8) | Job-volume-based service workflow | Small, device-compatible team | Service business | Needed device behavior or monthly job volume falls outside the demonstrated operating model | Full job on actual technician and office devices |
| [Tradify](#tradify) | Mobile inquiry-to-payment workflow | Smaller trade team | Trade service | A representative local invoice fails the live test | Local accounting entry from one representative invoice |
| [Fergus](#fergus) | Connected trade job management | Small trade contractor | Trade service | The demonstrated plan and user structure does not fit | Inquiry through payment with US support and plan boundaries |

Build one reusable demo pack before contacting vendors. Give every seller the same inputs:

- A common service job with an urgent reschedule, a return visit, parts used, field photos, customer approval, and an invoice.
- A recurring maintenance job with asset history, a checklist, a failed inspection item, follow-up work, and customer communication.
- A project or longer job with labor, materials, purchasing, progress billing, change handling, and a profitability report if that work matters to the business.
- A roster of current users and expected hires, split by office, field, management, subcontractor, and limited-access roles.
- Technician devices for hands-on field testing, a sample import file, and a map of accounting or ERP connections.
- A worksheet for package components, onboarding work, ongoing services, and likely expansion.

Use the buyer scorecard after pass-or-fail requirements remove obvious mismatches. Score the remaining tools across workflow fit, field usability, implementation effort, integration needs, reporting and control, pricing structure, and support. Define each condition before a demo, keep evidence beside every score, and carry unresolved issues into the next round instead of treating them as assumptions.

| Criterion | Evidence to collect | Pass signal |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow depth | One real job traced from intake through payment | Required handoffs work without duplicate entry |
| Integrations and data | System map, data owners, import and export test | Required records move with clear ownership |
| Implementation effort | Named owner, timeline, migration, training plan | Work and accountability fit available capacity |
| Field adoption | Technician test on actual devices and conditions | Core steps stay clear in the field |
| Reporting and control | Sample dashboards, exceptions, permissions | Each role gets actionable visibility |
| Pricing and total cost | Written quote, add-ons, services, renewal terms | Current and future costs are comparable |
| Support | Channels, hours, onboarding, escalation path | Support matches operational risk |

Keep two or three finalists. Ask each vendor to demonstrate the same jobs, exceptions, integrations, and reports. Treat every unresolved item as a condition, not an assumption.
